book.title: Think and Grow Rich (Düşün ve Zengin Ol)
book.author: Napoleon Hill

confidence_note: Andrew Carnegie is central to the book. Hill credits Carnegie with passing on the 'secret' and with urging him to organize a philosophy of achievement. Hill also presents Carnegie as a model of a definite purpose and of the Master Mind principle, meaning his results came through a group of associates rather than his own technical knowledge. The biographical details in the reference text are well-established history but are probably not recounted step by step in the book: emigrating from Scotland in 1848 as a boy, then working in a cotton mill, as a telegraph operator and on the railroad. Treat them as background. Several details are omitted as unverified or invented: 'not even five cents in his pocket', the self-question 'what will people need most?', the $480 million sale figure and the '~$14 billion today' conversion. The reference text says his secret was not intelligence, luck or privilege, only a single goal. That reading is a simplification. Hill stresses definiteness of purpose combined with the Master Mind alliance.
facts: Andrew Carnegie was a Scottish-born immigrant who arrived in America as a boy from a poor family (historical background).
He worked his way up through ordinary jobs before building one of the largest steel businesses of his era (historical background).
Hill says Carnegie shared with him the 'secret' of achievement and encouraged him to organize a philosophy of success for others.
Hill presents Carnegie as an example of a definite major purpose, pursued persistently and focused on steel.

Hill attributes much of Carnegie's fortune to a 'Master Mind' group of associates working in harmony. Hill says Carnegie relied on these people's knowledge rather than his own expertise in steel making.
Carnegie's steel interests became part of the formation of United States Steel in 1901.
tension: A poor immigrant boy with no special advantages ends up among the richest men in the world. What actually made the difference?
opening_idea: Open on the boy arriving in a new country with nothing. Then ask what separated him from thousands of other poor immigrants who arrived the same way.

lessons.idea: A single definite major purpose concentrates effort that would otherwise scatter.
lessons.anchor: Carnegie committed himself to steel rather than chasing many ventures.

lessons.idea: You don't need to know everything. You need the right people around a clear aim.
lessons.anchor: Hill's Master Mind point: Carnegie's associates supplied the steel expertise he lacked.

lessons.idea: Humble starting points are not the deciding factor. Decision and persistence are.
lessons.anchor: The move from ordinary early jobs to steel magnate.

reflect: If you had to name one definite aim for the next few years, could you say it in one sentence?
Who are the two or three people whose knowledge would most advance that aim, and do you work with them?
reflect_final: What would you have to stop doing so you could give real time to your one main aim?

use_cases.situation: A team meeting where priorities keep multiplying and nothing gets finished.
use_cases.move: Ask: 'If we could only deliver one thing this quarter, which one?' Then park the rest in writing.

use_cases.situation: A mentoring conversation with someone who says they lack the skills to pursue a goal.
use_cases.move: Ask them to list the people who already have those skills and how they could team up with one of them this month.

use_cases.situation: Planning your own week while feeling pulled in many directions.
use_cases.move: Write your one definite aim at the top of the week's plan and block the first hour of each day for it before anything else.

pocket_idea: Pick one definite aim, then surround it with people who know what you don't.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Carnegie reportedly didn't know much about making steel; he knew who did.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: A poor Scottish immigrant boy commits to one industry, gathers a group of capable associates and becomes a steel titan. Hill uses him to argue for definite purpose plus a 'Master Mind' alliance.
conversation_variants.question_idea: Is your biggest obstacle a lack of skill, or a lack of one clear aim and the people to pursue it with?
conversation_variants.key_contrast_idea: Scattered effort with solo expertise, versus one fixed aim powered by other people's knowledge.
